candidates.name: Everyday English Listening Podcast (niched to one learner pain-point)
candidates.niche: Faceless 'podcast-style' English listening practice for B1-B2 ESL learners — scripted two-voice conversations with on-screen subtitles, targeting a specific pain point ('understand English but can't speak', English for job interviews / healthcare workers / travel)
candidates.format: 15-22 min two-voice scripted dialogue episodes, AI or recorded voices, full on-screen subtitles, simple static/animated background; 3-5 uploads/week
candidates.why_now: English-learning podcasts were flagged as a 21x-growth faceless niche for 2026 in TubeLab's ranked niche data (via search snippet), and YouTube API data confirms multiple young faceless channels breaking out in 2024-2026 with modest production. The format monetizes global demand that never expires.

demand_evidence.finding: Channel created 2024-01-22, now 809,000 subs / 25.5M views / 381 videos (API, retrieved 2026-07-12). Recent uploads (Mar-Apr 2026) pull 11k-47k views each per videos.list — demand is current, not a one-time spike.

demand_evidence.title: YouTube Data API: VOA Learn English Through Stories
demand_evidence.finding: Channel created 2023-03-06 reached 258,000 subs / 6.6M views with only 21 videos (API) — evidence that a tiny catalog can win in this niche via evergreen search/suggested traffic.

competitor_scan.notes: Created Jan 2024; 25.5M total views; faceless conversational-podcast format; consistent 11k-47k views on Apr 2026 uploads. THE attainable-competition proof: <2.5 years old.
Created Mar 2023; 258k subs from just 21 videos, 6.6M views; single uploads at 40k-115k views.
Created 2022; 1.7M views / 938 videos — mid-tier is viable; niche not winner-take-all.
Created 2021, 146k views / 241 videos — counter-example showing generic execution stalls; differentiation (specific pain point, quality scripts) matters.

candidates.monetization_notes: AdSense on long watch-time videos (podcast format = high average view duration). Caveat (inference): audience is largely non-US/EU ESL learners, so RPM is likely low ($1-4 est., unverified) — volume play. Strong secondary monetization: language-app affiliates, own PDF/Anki study packs, channel memberships. Feedspot/industry lists confirm a large sponsor ecosystem (Preply, FluentU, etc. actively market in this space).
candidates.production_complexity: Low-medium for a solo creator: original dialogue scripts (LLM-assisted, human-edited for level-appropriate vocabulary), 2 AI voices, subtitle render, static visual. 3-5 episodes/week feasible. Deep well: unlimited daily-life/职业 scenarios — 100+ videos trivially.
candidates.originality_defense: Every episode is an originally scripted dialogue engineered for a CEFR level and a specific speaking pain point — original writing and pedagogy, not compilation or reused content. Differentiation vs. incumbents: pick one under-served segment (e.g., English for healthcare workers or job interviews) rather than generic 'daily conversation'.
candidates.risks: Low RPM per view (global audience); LEP's success has already triggered copycats — generic 'daily English podcast' positioning may be crowded by launch (inference); AI-voice-only channels must meet YouTube's July 2025 inauthentic-content bar via original scripts and consistent persona.

candidates.risks: Content decays fast (tool UIs change monthly) — little evergreen back-catalog; generic 'AI news' sub-lane is genuinely crowded (TheAIGRID/AI Search + many more), so a new entrant must niche by audience; hype-cycle exposure if AI ad spend cools.

candidates.name: Evidence-Based Aging Well (senior health, done credibly)
candidates.niche: Faceless explainer channel for 60+ viewers on mobility, nutrition, sleep, medication literacy — rigorously sourced (citing real studies/geriatric guidance) in a niche currently dominated by AI misinformation farms
candidates.format: 10-15 min narrated explainers with medical illustrations/B-roll, large text, slow pacing tuned for older viewers; cited sources on screen
candidates.why_now: Senior health was flagged at 19x growth for 2026 (TubeLab snippet), and a McGill Office for Science and Society investigation (surfaced via search snippet) documents AI content-farm videos targeting seniors ('Over 60?' titles) with a top video at 3.3M views — proof of massive under-served demand currently being captured by low-trust actors. YouTube's Feb 2026 removals of 'AI slop' channels (per search snippet) are clearing exactly these incumbents.

demand_evidence.finding: COUNTER-EVIDENCE I could verify: two legit small channels are NOT breaking out — 'Senior Health 60+' (created 2024-06): 221 subs/17.5k views/56 videos; 'Seniors Health Channel' (created 2025-02): 438 subs/70.2k views/194 videos. The 3.3M-view winners appear to be the misinfo farms. Attainable competition for credible players is UNPROVEN by my API data.

competitor_scan.notes: Created 2024-06; 17.5k views / 56 videos — small legit entrant stalling.
Created 2025-02; 70.2k views / 194 videos — high output, weak traction; suggests generic execution fails while sensational farms win.

candidates.monetization_notes: High CPM potential: health/pharma/insurance advertisers target 60+ viewers; Medium-sourced claims of $15+ RPM and supplement/wellness affiliates (reliability C). YMYL classification means AdSense is sensitive to medical-accuracy signals — credible sourcing is also a monetization strategy.
candidates.production_complexity: Medium: research-heavy scripts (must cite real studies), AI narration + licensed illustration/B-roll. Deep well: 100+ topics easily (every condition, medication class, exercise, nutrition question for 60+).
candidates.originality_defense: The entire thesis is anti-slop: original research summaries with on-screen citations, fact-checked scripts, consistent named narrator persona — positioned explicitly against the content farms McGill documented. Not compilation; every script is original synthesis of real literature.
candidates.risks: HIGHEST-RISK candidate: (1) my own API data shows legit small channels failing while sensationalist farms win — the honest version may grow slowly; (2) YMYL/medical-misinfo enforcement risk if any claim is sloppy; (3) ethical burden of accuracy for a vulnerable audience; (4) the '19x growth' and '100k subs in 90 days' claims come from B/C-grade blogs and are unverified. Treat as high-upside/unproven.
